parameters.query:
select c.*, e.state as event_state, sd.name as school_district_name, s.name as school_name
from public.contacts c
left join public.events e on e.id = c.event_id
left join public.school_districts sd on sd.id = c.school_district_id
left join public.schools s on s.id = c.school_id
where c.id = $1;

parameters.content:
## pipeline-match-contact

The n8n replacement for local-agent/agent.mjs's matchingLoop -- claim -> research-contact -> match-contact -> finalize_contact_match, mirroring processContact's exact call order and finalize_contact_match's exact 19-parameter call, verbatim.

claim_pending_contacts($1,$2,$3) is called with the SAME constants agent.mjs hardcodes -- MAX_MATCH_ATTEMPTS=3, RETRY_DELAY_MINUTES=10, CLAIM_LIMIT=1 -- not configurable here any more than they were there. CLAIM_LIMIT=1 means this pipeline never fans out to more than one item per tick, so none of the zero-item/fan-out hazards other pipelines in this migration had to branch around apply here: a zero-row claim just means every downstream node receives 0 items and does nothing, which is already the correct behavior.

Fetch Contact With Joins reproduces agent.mjs's second query (.from('contacts').select('*, event:events(state), school_district:school_districts(name), school:schools(name))')) as one SQL LEFT JOIN instead of two Supabase calls -- confirmed event_id/school_district_id/school_id are the real FK column names via the live schema (information_schema.columns), not assumed from the PostgREST embed syntax alone, since this project's own gotchas doc warns embed hints don't always resolve the direction you'd expect for self-referencing FKs (not the case here, but the same discipline applied).

research-contact's full output object is passed into match-contact completely unchanged (researchOutput: {{ $json.data }}, typed object, no intermediate Set/transform node) -- this is not a shortcut, it's the explicit contract both skills document: research-contact says every input field is passed through unchanged in its output, and match-contact's own Input section describes its input as exactly research-contact's output shape. A transform node here would be the one place this migration silently disagreed with what both skill files already promise.

Two independent success gates (Research Succeeded?, Match Succeeded?), each false branch a plain NoOp -- a failure at either step leaves the contact exactly as claim_pending_contacts will see it again next tick (match_status still 'pending', match_attempts already incremented by the claim itself), the same graceful-degrade-to-retry behavior processContact gets for free by throwing and letting the poll loop's outer catch swallow it. Matches this project's rule 3 exactly: a validation failure is a pipeline failure, the row stays pending for a human, never half-written -- there is no path in this graph that calls Finalize Contact Match without a validated MatchOutput in hand.

Finalize Contact Match's queryReplacement is one expression evaluating to a real array, not a comma-joined string -- notes and glanceSummary routinely contain commas (and candidateMatches, JSON-stringified, almost always does), which is exactly the class of bug pipeline-contact-intent's own sticky note already flagged and fixed the same way. p_candidate_matches is explicitly JSON.stringify()'d before going over the wire since the Postgres node has no native array-of-objects-to-jsonb parameter type; Postgres coerces the resulting text parameter to jsonb by the function's declared parameter type, same as how supabase-js's own .rpc() call serialized it before shipping this migration.

p_research_confidence/p_person_verified are read from Call sub-research-contact's OWN item (not threaded through match-contact, which never receives or echoes them) -- both nodes read via $('Node Name').item rather than the immediate predecessor, safe here specifically because CLAIM_LIMIT=1 means exactly one item flows through this entire graph, never the after-a-Code-node-fan-out case this project's own pairedItem discipline warns about.

p_extraction_ok is computed inline exactly as agent.mjs does -- extraction_confidence == null || extraction_confidence === 'high' -- read from Fetch Contact With Joins' own item, not from anything match-contact/research-contact echo back (neither one carries extractionConfidence through as its own top-level concern; research-contact's output does pass an extractionConfidence field through per its own contract, but reading it from the original claimed row is more direct and avoids depending on that pass-through behavior for a safety-relevant computation).

This closes the loop this migration's Stage 5 was building toward: finalize_contact_match's auto-approve CASE guard (review_status/auto_approved flip to approved/true only when match_confidence='high' AND extraction_ok AND matched_zoho_account_id is not null AND research_confidence <> 'low') is the single most safety-critical piece of logic in the whole matching system, per this project's own documented incident history -- see the migration drafted alongside this workflow, 20260923180000_finalize_contact_match_account_level_and_glance_summary.sql, which recorded that guard's real (already-live, already-stricter-than-committed) shape before this pipeline could safely call it with confidence the committed migration and the live function actually agree.

No credential attached to either Postgres node -- n8n instance has zero credentials configured, see n8n/README.md. Both "Postgres (n8n pipeline)" placeholder names, matching every other pipeline in this migration.

INACTIVE / BUILD-ONLY (n8n migration Stage 5). Not run against production data. local-agent/matchingLoop remains the system of record until this pipeline passes the plan-mandated shadow verification (validate MatchOutput against a held-out set, shadow-run without writing, only then cut over).
